_comment: Asset registry — every reusable asset carries a classification (what it contains) and an approval (which lane it may be used in). The renderer refuses assets not approved for the lane requesting them. Classification is a HUMAN judgement recorded here; audit-assets.py only enforces what is written. Section is chosen by FILE EXTENSION, not by where the entry sits: .mp3 -> audio, .png/.jpg -> mascots, .mp4 -> scenes. An entry filed under the wrong section shows up as both UNREGISTERED and MISSING in the audit. See agent-fleet-roadmap.md agent 12 and the audio policy in reel-creation-pipeline.md.

_schema.classification: vocal | vocal+daf | ambience | instrumental | mascot | mascot-reference | scene
_schema.lanes: which lanes may use this asset: kids, adults, or both. An empty list means retired — approved for no lane, and the gate will block it.
_schema.verified: true once a human has listened to or viewed the asset and confirmed the classification. false = present but unconfirmed; the audit reports it.
_schema.notes: why it is classified this way, or why it was retired

m2963-windows.mp4.notes: Arched openings in a sun-warmed mud-brick courtyard wall, a tree beyond, dust drifting in the light. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s, image-to-video from FLUX still variant 1. MODE B. Opening beat for Sahih Muslim #2963. KNOWN WEAKNESS: the brief was two openings, one onto bare earth and one onto a garden, so the frame itself carried the hadith's comparison. FLUX smoothed it into a single pleasant courtyard across all three variants. Kept as ATMOSPHERE only; the comparison is carried by m2963-bowls. Do not re-use this clip expecting it to say anything about above and below.

m2963-bowls.mp4.notes: A plain bowl of dates and bread beside a second bowl standing empty, warm morning light, linen beneath. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s, image-to-video from FLUX still variant 3. MODE B. This clip CARRIES THE MATN — full against empty is the whole hadith, and it is the only one of the four that does. Variant 3 chosen over 1 (cooler, more modern) and 2 (the second vessel held tea, which destroys the contrast). Surfaces specified matte throughout: polished ceramic is how a face gets into a scene that forbids one, as on b2628-stall.

m2963-sandals.mp4.notes: A worn pair of leather sandals set down on a stone threshold, a plain wooden door standing open onto a dark interior. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s, image-to-video from FLUX still variant 3. MODE B. Humility beat. Variant 3 chosen for the open doorway, which gives depth and makes the sandals read as left behind rather than arranged; variant 2 had better light but a flatter frame.

m2963-room.mp4.notes: A woven reed mat on swept earth, a folded wool blanket, a rough clay water jar, low sun crossing the mat. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s, image-to-video from FLUX still variant 3. MODE B. Closing beat: sufficiency. REPLACED A FAILED CONCEPT — the fourth clip was to be stone steps shot looking DOWN, the hadith's instruction as camera direction. Six FLUX variants across two prompts all photographed the staircase from the bottom looking up, which states the opposite of the matn; the prior would not break and the concept was abandoned rather than paid for a third time. No lamp in frame: an open flame generated a temple shrine on b2654.

m2759-door-night.mp4.notes: A single-leaf wooden door standing open onto desert night in a recessed mud-brick alcove, moonlight across two worn stone steps. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s, image-to-video from FLUX 2 still m2759-door-night-r-1. MODE B. Opening beat for Sahih Muslim #2759. REGENERATED: all three original night stills hinged the door on the LEFT while the daylight stills hinged it RIGHT, which would have flipped the door mid-reel on a set whose whole claim is that the door never changes. The re-prompt states the hinge side explicitly. Kling ADDS A MOON over the clip that is not in the still - accepted here as a cropped background detail, but any re-use must re-check it against the splitting-of-the-moon collision.

m2759-threshold.mp4.notes: Close on the worn stone threshold at the darkest hour, a band of moonlight across the stone, dry leaves at the edge. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s, image-to-video from FLUX 2 still variant 3. MODE B. Second beat. The only clip of the four with no door leaf visible, so it reads neutral on hinge direction and can sit anywhere in the sequence. Variant 2 was rejected outright for a bright point light at the top of frame - that is how a lamp gets into a scene that must offer nothing standing in for the divine attribute.

m2759-firstlight.mp4.notes: The same doorway at first light, pale colourless sky beyond, the stone of the steps just becoming visible. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s, image-to-video from FLUX 2 still variant 3. MODE B. Third beat. KNOWN WEAKNESS: by 7s the light has run most of the way to gold, so the clip ends close to where m2759-dawn begins. Acceptable in sequence because it reads as time passing, but do not re-use it expecting a distinct pre-dawn state. The first attempt at this concept lost the alcove entirely - flat wall, wide horizon - because the prompt named the sky and not the architecture.

m2759-dawn.mp4.notes: The same doorway at sunrise, warm light pouring across the stone threshold, long shadows thrown inward. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s, image-to-video from FLUX 2 still variant 3. MODE B. Closing beat. The sun is visible in frame and that is deliberate - it is the hadith own final clause about the sun rising from its place of setting. FLUX returned a DOUBLE door on variant 2 of this prompt and again on the firstlight re-run: a door standing open carries a two-leaf prior, so single-leaf must be stated.

m2628-musk.mp4.notes: A small stoppered vial of dark musk resin on folded undyed linen in a shuttered perfumer's room at first light, dust drifting in the beam. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s, image-to-video. MODE B. Opening beat of the four-clip arc for Sahih Muslim #2628 — musk, the trade, the forge, the cloth. Variant 2 chosen: variants 1 and 3 carried floating orange specks that read as embers, which is the forge's visual language leaking into the musk scene. RENAMED b2628-musk.mp4 -> m2628-musk.mp4 on 2026-10-09 (P197): the clip is Sahih Muslim #2628 and carried a Bukhari prefix. Found by audit-assets --names, not by reading.

m2628-stall.mp4.notes: Rows of stoppered brass and blue glass vials on a worn shelf in an unoccupied early-Islamic market stall, backlit so the glass glows rather than mirrors the room. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s, image-to-video. MODE B. Variant 3 chosen: variants 1 and 2 came back as ornate fantasy potion shops, gold filigree and saturated apothecary glass, and only 3 reads as a working trade stall. Backlighting was specified deliberately — polished glass is how a face gets into a scene that forbids one. RENAMED b2628-stall.mp4 -> m2628-stall.mp4 on 2026-10-09 (P197): the clip is Sahih Muslim #2628 and carried a Bukhari prefix. Found by audit-assets --names, not by reading.

m2628-forge.mp4.notes: A blacksmith's open coal hearth and anvil in an empty workshop, smoke column rising and bending, embers pulsing. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s, image-to-video. MODE B. Variant 2 chosen for unmistakable tongs and period stonework. KNOWN COMPROMISE: no bellows in frame, though the matn's image is نافخ الكير, the blower of bellows — bellows with nobody working them read as furniture, and somebody working them breaks MODE B. The smoke carries the meaning and b2628-robes closes it. RENAMED b2628-forge.mp4 -> m2628-forge.mp4 on 2026-10-09 (P197): the clip is Sahih Muslim #2628 and carried a Bukhari prefix. Found by audit-assets --names, not by reading.

m2628-robes.mp4.notes: Two folded robes on a weathered wooden counter in the same shuttered room as b2628-musk: one clean pale linen, one charred black along the folds with embers still glowing and a thread of smoke lifting. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s, image-to-video. MODE B. Closing beat. Variant 2 chosen because it is the only one where the burn reads as BURNED — in the others the dark cloth could be dyed or merely sooty, which loses the whole contrast. Reached after four rounds: hanging-on-a-line variants were rejected for modern clothespins, and a lying-on-the-ground version for reading as a figure. RENAMED b2628-robes.mp4 -> m2628-robes.mp4 on 2026-10-09 (P197): the clip is Sahih Muslim #2628 and carried a Bukhari prefix. Found by audit-assets --names, not by reading.

b6857-still.mp4.notes: Still water in a worn stone basin before dawn, surface barely breathing. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s. MODE B. Opening beat of a four-clip arc — whole, ruined, first rain, restored. Source still was variant 1, the brighter caustic one; variant 3 was quieter and more natural but the operator judged the motion better on 1.

b6857-cracked.mp4.notes: Dried riverbed, one deep fissure running to the horizon, bleached under hard overhead light. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s. MODE B. The ruin beat — muubiqat are things that destroy. Chosen over two tighter crops because it reads as a watercourse, which makes it the same place as the other three clips rather than generic cracked ground.

b6857-firstrain.mp4.notes: Rain falling on dry cracked earth, drops darkening the dust, a soft curtain drifting across the distance. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s. MODE B. The turn back. Chosen over a variant whose drops fell in a straight vertical column, which would have animated synthetically.

b6857-flow.mp4.notes: Water running again over smooth dark stones, warm early light down the centre. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s. MODE B. Restoration, and it closes the set's tonal arc: cold blue, bleached, grey, warm. None of the seven sins is literalised anywhere in this set — deliberate, after b2654 where a lamp in a niche generated a temple shrine and a fracturing reflection generated the moon splitting.

b2654-ripples.mp4.notes: Stone basin of still water in an empty pre-dawn courtyard, three drops falling in sequence, rings overlapping. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s, generate_audio off. MODE B. Carries the question asked three times. Architecture reads as a Roman cloister rather than anything Islamic — ambiguous, accepted.

b2654-dawn-v3.mp4.notes: Vast empty dunes at first light, one sun clearing the horizon. Kling 2.6 Pro 10s. MODE B. Third attempt at the shirk beat: a lamp in a niche generated a temple shrine, and a fracturing reflection generated the moon splitting, which collides with a different hadith. Depicts tawhid rather than shirk, so there is nothing to literalise wrongly.
